**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Generate fallback IDs only when React.useId is unavailable**

`fallbackRef` is initialized with `generateId(baseId)` before the `reactId` branch, so in React 18+ every `useId` call still mutates the global ID factory even though that value is never returned. Because `generateId` registers each issued ID in the process-wide registry, repeated mounts in long-lived SPA/SSR runtimes accumulate unused IDs and continuously advance counters, which creates avoidable memory/counter drift. Compute the fallback lazily only when `React.useId()` is missing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid dispatching outside-click handler for overlapping events**

Registering `mousedown`, `touchstart`, and `pointerdown` together causes one physical interaction to invoke the callback multiple times on browsers that emit both legacy and pointer events (e.g., mouse click => `pointerdown` + `mousedown`). For dismiss handlers this can duplicate `onOpenChange` side effects and can break consumers that toggle state in the callback. Use one event family (or dedupe by pointer type) so each interaction is handled once.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Position scrollbar thumb in track coordinates**

The thumb offset is computed as a percentage of remaining track space, but it is applied with `translateY(...%)`, where percentage transforms are relative to the thumb’s own size instead of the track. This makes the thumb travel too short a distance (and not reach the visual end at max scroll), especially when the thumb is large. Apply offset in track-relative units (e.g., `top/left` percent or px) to keep thumb position aligned with scroll state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
